subject: CHANGES REQUESTED S13 @745f1f6f: offline Reader crash on lazy chunks (critical), no handwriting-OCR opt-out UI, stale offline edits overwrite newer ones, paste CSP errors, WebKit smoke red (38/44, 39/44)
body:
Reviewer: review13. Reviewed head 745f1f6f (claude/naadi-shared), ledger done 20261117T121901. Ran everything locally, on loopback stacks only (pg/storage/auth containers *-review13 and *-review13e). The hosted DB and Spaces were not touched. VERDICT: CHANGES REQUESTED. Defects 1–3 block approval. Defects 4–6 must be fixed in this segment. 7–9 are minor. LOCAL RESULTS - Unit pytest (-m "not live and not db"): 1756 passed, 1 skipped. - vitest: 738 web + 133 shared + 75 ink, all passed. Lint (biome + ruff + format): clean. Typecheck (tsc + mypy): clean. - db pytest (fresh stack): 662 passed, 4 failed, 3 skipped. None of the 4 is in S13 code (see "Not S13" below). - Smoke set, notes.spec + notebooks.spec, with --retries=0 --workers=2 on webkit-ipad-portrait, webkit-ipad-landscape, webkit-phone-390 and chromium-laptop-1440: - Run 1: 38/44. - Run 2: 39/44. - All failures are WebKit. chromium-laptop-1440 passed 11/11 in both runs. notes.spec:426 (prod CSP) passed on all 4 projects in both runs. - Probes (a temporary spec, deleted afterwards): pasting hostile HTML into the page-notes editor on the APP_ENV=prod server; selection-toolbar placement on touch. DEFECTS 1. [CRITICAL] Going offline on the Reader before the lazy highlight engine has loaded crashes the whole page to the root "Something went wrong!" screen. - Where: apps/web/src/highlights/HighlightableText.tsx:7 and :60-64 (lazy HighlightEngine inside Suspense, with no error boundary). Same pattern at apps/web/src/notes/ReaderNotes.tsx:8 (PageNotesPanel) and apps/web/src/notes/PageNotesPanel.tsx:25 (NoteEditor). - Cause: there is no precache yet (vite.config.ts:97, no globPatterns; that arrives in S18). A chunk that hasn't been fetched is unreachable offline. The rejected import() propagates to the router error component. - Repro: notes.spec.ts:344 on webkit-ipad-landscape failed in BOTH runs, at selectWords :355. The screenshot is the root error page (.tmp/r13/pw1/notes-highlights-notes-and-3a49c-*/test-failed-1.png). - Manual repro: open /learn/ch01/ch01-s02, go offline within about 1 s → the page crashes. Or: stay online with the page-notes panel never opened, go offline, select text, tap Note → the PageNotesPanel import fails the same way. - This regressed with 745f1f6f/57ff7dad. Before those commits the engine and editor were in the reader's static graph. - Fix: wrap each lazy chunk in an error boundary that degrades (content stays readable; the toolbar or panel shows the offline copy with a retry). Also prefetch the engine, panel and editor chunks right after first paint, so they are cached before the student can go offline. 2. [HIGH, privacy] There is no UI for the handwriting-search opt-out. Ink images go to the free vision model by default, and the student cannot turn that off. - The API, the ui_copy keys and the server path all exist: auth_routes.py:381, ink/ocr/queue.py, app_config.yaml:1912-1914 (ink.ocr.setting_label/note/cleared). - But nothing in apps/web uses them. `grep -rn "ink.ocr.setting\|handwriting_search" apps/web/src` → 0 hits. InkSettingsPage.tsx has no toggle. - The S13 spec says: "Settings toggle 'Handwriting search (sends ink images to the AI model)', default on; off → no runs and the existing text is cleared." The brief also says notes and ink must never reach an LLM without explicit user consent. As shipped, the default is on with no way to turn it off. - Fix: add the toggle to Settings → Pencil & ink (PATCH /api/me settings.handwriting_search), with an e2e that turning it off clears recognised_text and stops runs. - Lead decision needed: whether OCR should default to off until the student opts in. 3. [HIGH, data loss] Offline sync of notes and notebook pages is last-ARRIVAL-wins, with no time bound. A stale offline edit silently overwrites a newer edit from another device. - Where: apps/web/src/notes/api.ts:115 (transport.update sends only the fields), apps/web/src/notes/outbox.ts:207-224 and apps/web/src/notebooks/outbox.ts. Neither queue sends if_updated_at or an edit timestamp. - On the server, routes.py:406 has an if_updated_at guard that no client uses. - Repro: device A goes offline and edits the page note of section S at 10:00 ("A"). Device B, online, edits the same note at 11:00 ("B"), which saves. A reconnects at 12:00 → flushOps sends A's whole body → the server stores "A", and B's newer text is gone with no conflict shown. - This is not what the S12b model requires (LWW by edit time, client clock clamped to server time + 5 min, ink/store.py:26). - Fix: send the edit time, or the base updated_at, with each queued patch. The server keeps the newer row, bounded by server time, as in S12b; or it returns 409 note_conflict and the client keeps both versions (for example a "conflict copy"). - Needs an e2e with two contexts. 4. [MEDIUM, CSP/console] Pasting ordinary rich text into any TipTap note editor logs CSP errors on the prod server and sends CSP reports. - Pasted HTML is parsed by ProseMirror's clipboard readHTML (innerHTML on a detached document; built chunk dist-*.js line 10). Every style="…" attribute in the paste triggers a style-src-attr violation. - Chromium: "Applying inline style violates … 'style-src 'self''" ×2. WebKit: "Refused to apply a stylesheet…" ×2, plus POSTs to /api/csp-report. - Almost any copy from a web page or Word carries style attributes. - The sanitising itself is good. After pasting
